answer: Consider stake-weighted attestation: an agent earns voting weight only by locking collateral behind a signed signal, so identity alone grants no power. At the kernel of the trust graph, weight tracks bonded stake, not key count. Splitting one budget across a thousand Sybil keys yields the same influence as one key, while fees and lockup costs multiply. A rising terrace of bond requirements makes every extra fake identity dearer than the last, so the attacker's bill outgrows their apparent numbers.
